questions.question: What does Malevolent Shrine look like?
questions.subject: Malevolent Shrine

answer.item: Befitting its name, Malevolent Shrine constructs a disfeatured Buddhist shrine (resembling an oversized zushi, or more vaguely a chinjudō) that has been distorted to instead enshrine demons. Several bovine skulls form the base of the shrine.

questions.question: What does the roof of Malevolent Shrine look like?
questions.subject: Malevolent Shrine

answer.item: The hip-and-gable roof is crowned with a small bovine skull, has horns emerging from it, two smaller mouths in each gable, tiny fanged mouths in each of the top corners of the entrances' doorframes, as well as human skulls that hang down from the four corners of the roof.

questions.question: How are the entrances to Malevolent Shrine formed?
questions.subject: Malevolent Shrine

answer.item: The four entrances to the shrine are formed by four large, grotesque mouths, complete with humanlike teeth and tongues.

questions.question: What does Malevolent Shrine's alternate form look like?
questions.subject: Malevolent Shrine

answer.item: In its alternate form, Malevolent Shrine takes a much more gruesome, warped and eldritch appearance. It takes the form of a large mass of flesh, horns and teeth with multiple eyes - one large, central eye surrounded by six smaller eyes - that stare in different directions.

questions.question: How does Malevolent Shrine's sure-hit effect work?
questions.subject: Malevolent Shrine

answer.item: Malevolent Shrine's sure-hit sure-kill effect relentlessly slashes apart anything until nothing but dust remains of what has been caught in the effective range, via Sukuna's two types of slashing attacks: Cleave and Dismantle, which only cease when the domain is disengaged or Sukuna is so badly injured he cannot sustain the domain anymore.

questions.question: How does Malevolent Shrine decide which slash hits a target?
questions.subject: Malevolent Shrine

answer.item: Dismantle strikes targets without cursed energy while Cleave slashes targets with it.

questions.question: How far can Sukuna expand Malevolent Shrine's effective range?
questions.subject: Malevolent Shrine

answer.item: Sukuna has the divine ability to expand his domain without closing the barrier to create a separate space, manifesting it in the existing airspace instead. This creates a binding vow due to allowing escape from the domain that enables him to expand the effective range of the sure-hit up to a maximum radius of nearly 200 meters.

questions.question: Why can Malevolent Shrine not be destroyed by normal means?
questions.subject: Malevolent Shrine

answer.item: Furthermore, unlike other domains which operate with an outer shell like Unlimited Void and can be cancelled if the shell is destroyed, Malevolent Shrine cannot be destroyed by any normal means because of the lack of an enclosed barrier. The only way to effectively destroy Malevolent Shrine is to injure Sukuna to the point where he can no longer maintain the domain.

questions.question: How did Sukuna first use Malevolent Shrine against a Finger Bearer?
questions.subject: Malevolent Shrine

answer.item: Sukuna is a master of domain expansion and his Malevolent Shrine is equally refined as Satoru Gojo's Unlimited Void, capable of overpowering the vast majority of domains. With the power of only three fingers, Sukuna effortlessly cut a Finger Bearer, a special grade cursed spirit, to pieces immediately after opening Malevolent Shrine.

questions.question: What damage did Malevolent Shrine cause in Shibuya during Sukuna's fight with Mahoraga?
questions.subject: Malevolent Shrine

answer.item: He set Malevolent Shrine to target anything within range with cursed energy using Cleave and used Dismantle for anything without. This not only injured Mahoraga, but also massacred numerous civilians and cut off Toge Inumaki's arm as a result.

questions.question: How did Malevolent Shrine clash with Unlimited Void inside a barrier?
questions.subject: Malevolent Shrine

answer.item: As previously mentioned, Malevolent Shrine can equal Unlimited Void in a domain clash, but that is only the case inside a barrier. Malevolent Shrine's range reached beyond Unlimited Void's barrier during the first clash of domains. With a domain's barrier being weak to attacks on its outer shell, Gojo's domain was crushed by Malevolent Shrine's slashing attacks and he was immediately struck by its sure-hit slashes.

questions.question: What binding vow did Sukuna make to counter Gojo's reinforced domain barrier?
questions.subject: Malevolent Shrine

answer.item: Later in the fight, Sukuna revealed that he can change the conditions of his domain with a binding vow, such as removing Malevolent Shrine's sure-hit effect within Unlimited Void's effective area and narrowing down its effective range similar to when it was used in Shibuya in exchange for increased power to counter Gojo's Unlimited Void's reinforced outer shell, collapsing it a second time.

questions.question: What happened in the third exchange of domains between Sukuna and Gojo?
questions.subject: Malevolent Shrine

answer.item: On the third exchange, due to Gojo also changing his domain's condition in response, both domains collapsed simultaneously after three minutes due to Malevolent Shrine destroying Unlimited Void's barrier from the outside, but Gojo managing to damage Sukuna enough to the point where he can't maintain his domain.

questions.question: How did Sukuna's delay in activating his domain let Gojo wound him?
questions.subject: Malevolent Shrine

answer.item: As Gojo punched Sukuna into a pillar, both fighters activated their domain expansions once more. However, Sukuna activated his less than one-hundredth of a second later due to having to heal his physical body using reverse cursed technique, thus delaying him from restoring his cursed technique. As a result, Unlimited Void was able to briefly immobilize him, allowing Gojo to severely wound him.

questions.question: Why did Sukuna's final full attempt to expand Malevolent Shrine against Gojo fail?
questions.subject: Malevolent Shrine

answer.item: However, upon expanding Malevolent Shrine, it immediately collapsed as a result of the damage done to Sukuna's brain by Unlimited Void, which he was subjected to for a total of less than ten seconds.

questions.question: How did Sukuna unleash an impromptu Malevolent Shrine after Yuji's Black Flashes?
questions.subject: Malevolent Shrine

answer.item: After suffering seven consecutive Black Flashes from Yuji Itadori, Sukuna activated an impromptu Malevolent Shrine as a desperate measure. By changing the hand signs and using a part of his brain undamaged by Unlimited Void, Sukuna was able to unleash Malevolent Shrine with its full effective area and output while being invigorated with the effects of his earlier rush of Black Flashes by including uncertain conditions and improvised binding vows.

questions.question: How long could Sukuna keep his impromptu Malevolent Shrine active?
questions.subject: Malevolent Shrine

answer.item: Due to Sukuna's condition, he could only maintain this high-level domain for 99 seconds before it crumbled.

questions.question: How did Sukuna adapt Malevolent Shrine against Yuta's Unlimited Void?
questions.subject: Malevolent Shrine

answer.item: In order to counter the increased durability of Unlimited Void's barrier, Sukuna shrunk the effective range of his domain to only surround the outer shell of Yuta's domain, thereby removing the time limit.

questions.question: How did Sukuna try to expand his domain after his cursed technique was burnt out?
questions.subject: Malevolent Shrine

answer.item: In response, he performed a highly risky maneuver and reset his burnt-out cursed technique. Regaining his cursed technique, the King of Curses attempted to expand his domain one more time.

questions.question: What prevented Sukuna's final domain expansion during his fight with Yuji?
questions.subject: Malevolent Shrine

answer.item: However, he was damaged by Nobara Kugisaki's Resonance before he could activate the technique, causing him to disengage his anti-domain technique's hand signs.

questions.question: What hand sign does Sukuna make to expand Malevolent Shrine?
questions.subject: Malevolent Shrine

answer.item: To expand Malevolent Shrine, Sukuna makes the so-called Enma Palm Sign 閻魔天の掌印 Enmaten no Shōin:(Chapter 255) the two-handed mudra representing the Buddhist god of death.

questions.question: What does the name Fukuma in Malevolent Shrine's Japanese name refer to?
questions.subject: Malevolent Shrine

answer.item: Fukuma 伏魔, comes from fukumaden 伏魔殿, referring to an abode of demons or a palace wherein demons lurk, and is also translatable as "Pandemonium".

questions.question: Which real-world shrine does Malevolent Shrine resemble?
questions.subject: Malevolent Shrine

answer.item: The shrine this domain summons (especially with its hip-and-gable roof and four openings) superficially resembles the zushi-style Tamamushi Shrine 玉虫厨子 Tamamushi no Zushi of the Hōryū Temple.

questions.question: What forms the base of the Malevolent Shrine?
questions.subject: Malevolent Shrine

answer.item: Several bovine skulls form the base of the shrine.

questions.question: What stands at each corner of the Malevolent Shrine?
questions.subject: Malevolent Shrine

answer.item: Four short, tree-like stumps with gnarled branches stand at each corner of the shrine.

questions.question: What other features does Malevolent Shrine's alternate form have?
questions.subject: Malevolent Shrine

answer.item: There are also patches of hair-like appendages throughout its body, along with four large curved horns at the top, two giant humanoid hands at the bottom and a spine-like appendage tapering down from the back.

questions.question: What can the word Mizushi in the shrine's name mean?
questions.subject: Malevolent Shrine

answer.item: could have different meanings depending on context, both as an archaic word for "Kitchen" or as a word for "Shrine"
